candidates.why: The same haftarah verses (I Kings 1:5-6) read as self-satisfied pride: Adoniyahu 'סובר שהוא כבר איש תם וישר', so God sent him no humbling grief. It adds that even the crown one gives Hashem is His ('כתר כל הכתרים'). This is the same diagnosis and close to the maamar's crowning theme, although it reads 'ולא עצבו' differently.

found.ref: Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 1
found.why: Explains the same Zohar: the truly great (Moshe) holds himself small, and the small hold themselves great. The higher level is nearer to unity, and the first three (ג"ר) lie above the seven days of building, which matches Rav Tzadok's 100/20/7 mapping.

Maharal on Chullin 89a: Israel's greatness is divine, so the more of it they have, the humbler they become; the nations' greatness is physical, so they grow proud. This is exactly the maamar's Israel/nations section.
Joins the same Zohar ('מאן דאיהו זעיר איהו רב') with Sotah 5a ('אין אני והוא'): because Moshe was humble the Shechinah dwelt with him, and what 'לית ליה מגרמיה כלום' receives all blessing.

Reads 'באים בימים' as 'עאלו ביומין עלאין': Avraham and Sarah could not bear children until they entered the supernal days. This is the maamar's reason why Yitzchak's birth needed parents already refined in the first three.

footnotes.text:
**Yakar MiPaz, Haftarah of Chayei Sarah** (Chassidus) — Also reads Adoniyahu's flaw as the pride of one who thinks himself already perfect, and adds that even the crown a person gives Hashem is Hashem's own. It differs on "ולא עצבו": Hashem sent him no humbling grief, while Rav Tzadok says David never had cause to rebuke him.
"מתנשא לאמר אני אמלוך שסובר שהוא כבר איש תם וישר"

footnotes.ref: Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 1
footnotes.text:
**Zera Kodesh, Chayei Sarah 1** (Chassidus) — On the same Zohar: the truly great, like Moshe, holds himself small. The higher a level, the nearer it is to Divine unity, so the first three sefiros take the singular "year" and the seven days of building the plural. This is close to Rav Tzadok's mapping of Sarah's years.
"מאן דאיהו רב מחזיק עצמו לזעיר כי כן מצינו במשה רבינו"

**Maharal, Netivot Olam, Netiv HaAnavah 2** (Machshava) — On Chullin 89a: Israel's greatness is divine, so the more of it they receive, the humbler they become. The nations' greatness is physical, so it makes them prouder. This is Rav Tzadok's contrast of Avraham, Moshe and David with Nimrod and Nevuchadnetzar.
"כל עוד שהגדולה יותר בישראל והם יותר מגיעים אל מדריגה אלקית נמצא בהם הענוה יותר והם ממעטין עצמם"

**Sefat Emet, Beha'aloscha (Sefaria 24:2)** (Chassidus) — Joins "מאן דאיהו זעיר איהו רב" with Sotah 5a ("אין אני והוא יכולין לדור"): the Shechinah dwelt with Moshe because of his humility, and what "לית ליה מגרמיה כלום" receives every blessing. Rav Tzadok draws the same chain here: lowliness, then becoming a dwelling for the Shechinah.
"שהי' עניו מאוד שרתה עמו השכינה ומדברת מתוך גרונו"

**R. Chaim Vital, Sha'ar Ma'amarei Rashbi, Introduction 41** (Kabbalah) — Reads "זקנים באים בימים" as entry into the supernal days. Avraham and Sarah could not bear children before that, which matches Rav Tzadok's point that Yitzchak's soul needed parents already refined in the first three.
"כי לא היו ראוים לילד עד הכנסם בימים העליונים האלו"
